# FastAPI-Restly

> **Class-based REST resources for FastAPI and SQLAlchemy. Minimal boilerplate, full control.**

The Guide has one page for each part of Restly, in five groups. Each page
starts with how that part works, then shows how to use it. If you are new to
Restly, start with the tutorial, [Build a Blog API](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/tutorial.html).

The goal of Restly is less boilerplate and more consistency.

In Restly, you write your API as view classes. A view is a class that groups
related FastAPI routes, for example all routes under `/projects`. The base
class, `fr.View`, is for your own set of
reusable endpoints. It has no predefined routes. See
[Group endpoints that are not CRUD](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/views.html#when-to-use-view-directly).

`fr.RestView` is a view that already
has five CRUD routes. You give it a SQLAlchemy model, and it serves routes to
list, read, create, update and delete rows of that model. `RestView` has an
async version, `fr.AsyncRestView`.
These docs say `RestView` for both.

```python
@fr.include_view(app)
class ProjectView(fr.AsyncRestView):
    prefix = "/projects"
    model = Project  # your SQLAlchemy model
```

Each route of a `RestView` has two layers that you can change:

- **The HTTP layer**: one endpoint method for each route, such as
  `update_endpoint`. It holds what is about HTTP: the path, the parameters
  and the response. To change one option of a route, such as the status
  code, use `fr.modify_route`. To
  change more, replace the endpoint method. See
  [Change one option of a route](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/crud_routes.html#modify-route).
- **The business layer**: business methods, such as `create`, `update` and
  `delete`. They make the change to the data. Override one to change what a
  route does, for example to hash a password or to set a field. See
  [Change what a write does](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/crud_routes.html#business-methods).

Between the two layers, Restly runs a fixed set of steps, such as loading a
row from the database, checking access and committing.
[How a CRUD route runs](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/crud_routes.html#view-request-steps) shows all steps in order, and
which ones you can override.

Some things you write only once:

- **Fields**: you list the fields that clients see in one Pydantic schema, and
  Restly builds the create, update and response schemas from it. If you do not
  write this schema, Restly makes one from the model.
- **Access**: you write once which rows a caller can see, as a scope, and
  Restly applies it to every read of the model.
- **Shared behavior**: behavior that several views share goes in a base view
  that they inherit from.

Underneath, Restly is plain FastAPI, SQLAlchemy and Pydantic. Your model stays
your own SQLAlchemy model, the routes are FastAPI routes, and the schemas are
Pydantic classes. When a route does not fit Restly, write it as a normal
FastAPI route next to your views.

## Tutorial

- [Tutorial: Build a Blog API](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/tutorial.html)
- [Tutorial: Add Authors and Drafts](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/tutorial_customizing.html)

## Setup

- [New Projects](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/new_projects.html): start a project with `restly new`, lay it out as it grows, and serve more than one API version.
- [Existing Projects](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/existing_projects.html): add Restly to an app that you already have, share its login check and its `get_db`, keep its engine and models, and replace a hand-written router with a view.
- [Database & Configuration](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/database.html): tell Restly where its database is, reuse the engine, sessionmaker or session generator that your app already has, use another database on one view, such as a read replica, and open a session outside a request.
- [Models](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/models.html): add Restly's defaults and common columns to your models, and set the values that every write needs, such as the author or a slug.

## Views & Routes

- [Views](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/views.html): the view classes, how to declare routes, add a decorator and register a view, routes that are not CRUD, such as login and webhooks, and how views share behavior through base classes.
- [React Admin](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/react_admin.html): connect react-admin to a view, the list format and the routes that react-admin expects, to-many id arrays, CORS, and a list that shows no rows.
- [Type Annotations](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/typing.html): type the schema, the methods that you override and your custom routes.

## CRUD Routes

- [Overview](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/crud_routes.html): the five default routes, the id type, how a route runs, async or sync, how to change one option of a route, leave some routes out, where a business method fits, and how to replace an endpoint method.
- [List](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/crud_list.html): the steps of `GET /`, what you can change, a header with the total, and a list of a subset.
- [Get One](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/crud_get_one.html): the steps of `GET /{id}`, visibility and policy, a row found by a slug or a composite key, and the error for a missing row.
- [Create](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/crud_create.html): the steps of `POST /`, the `create` method, a password hash, the id of a new row, and a `Location` header.
- [Update](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/crud_update.html): the steps of `PATCH /`, what you can change, the`update` method, a `PUT` route, and an update from a custom route.
- [Delete](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/crud_delete.html): the steps of `DELETE /`, the`delete` method, a soft delete, and a response with the deleted row.
- [Custom Routes](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/custom_routes.html): routes of your own on a CRUD view, a lookup by another key, actions such as publish, and several rows in one action.
- [Commits & Hooks](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/commits.html): what commits and when, code before or after the commit, work after the response, errors in a write, several writes in one commit, code that must commit, and the same logic in a script or a worker.
- [Nested Routes](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/nested_routes.html): serve a child resource under its parent, create a child, limit the parents that a client can reach, and nest more than one level.

## Requests & Responses

- [Schemas & Validation](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/schemas.html): generate the schema or write it, keep a field out of the requests or the responses, validate input, keep times in UTC, keep NaN and infinity, store a Pydantic model in a JSON column, use other field names in JSON, such as camelCase, and build a class for each view with `SchemaType`.
- [Relationships](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/relationships.html): accept the id of another row, check that the row exists, link many rows to many rows, return related objects, and fix `MissingGreenlet`.
- [Responses](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/responses.html): what each route returns, the list envelope and the list response schema, the response of a custom route, and how to change the shape of one route or of all routes.
- [Filtering, Sorting & Pagination](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/filtering.html): the filters, the sort order and the pages that a client can use on a list, the keys that a view chooses, filters of your own, and list params that you write yourself.
- [Errors](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/errors.html): raise a 404 or a 403, see why a duplicate value gives a 409, and change the error body.
- [OpenAPI](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/openapi.html): the tags, names and operation IDs of the routes, and how to document a custom route.

## Access

- [Request Context](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/context.html): bind the current user in a dependency, a script or a test.
- [Authorization](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/authorization.html): allow or refuse each action, for each caller.
- [Query Clauses](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/clauses.html): name a query rule once, then reuse and combine it.
- [Scopes](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/scopes.html): hide rows from every read, show each user only their own rows, and soft-delete rows.
- [Multi-Tenancy](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/tenancy.html): keep the rows of each tenant apart.

## Testing & Deploying

- [Testing](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/testing.html): set up the test suite, build the test schema, and use the test clients and fixtures.
- [Deploying](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/deploying.html): read the settings from the environment, run the app, set up Alembic, add a health check, and check the list settings before an API goes public.

## What FastAPI covers

- [Security](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/security/): OAuth2, API keys and other security schemes. To make the caller available to your views, see [Request Context](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/context.html#current-request-binding).
- [Middleware](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/middleware/).
- [CORS](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/cors/). For a react-admin frontend, see also [CORS for React Admin](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/react_admin.html#react-admin-cors).
- [Background tasks](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/background-tasks/). For work that must still happen after a crash, use an outbox row in a [transaction hook](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/commits.html#after-action-commit-raises).
- [File uploads](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/request-files/).
- [WebSockets](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/advanced/websockets/). Declare them on the app or on a router, not on a view: a view has HTTP routes only.
